findings.issue_text: Partial-failure dead end: DB write commits before calendar update; if updateCalendarAttendees throws, retry is impossible because dedupe filter strips already-persisted guests and throws misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error; no transaction or compensation path
Guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings: neither handler nor UI checks booking.status, sending CONFIRMED calendar invites for dead events and 'Guests Added' emails to organizer
Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so attendees adding guests fail or silently no-op against the organizer's calendar event
Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||, collapsing to owner-only access and blocking team admins who are not owners

Case-sensitive duplicate and blacklist checks: raw email comparison allows blacklist bypass via case variation and duplicate attendee records via case-differing emails; same flaw exists client-side in AddGuestsDialog
Server schema doesn't enforce email uniqueness within the guests array, so direct API callers can create duplicate attendee rows; uniqueness invariant only exists in client-side schema
Email-send failures are swallowed: caught error is never logged with context, no error reporting fires, and handler returns success message regardless of email failure
isInvalidEmail flag is never reset on input change, success, or cancel, so the invalid-email error banner persists across fixes and dialog reopens

Error toast fallback is dead code: template literal always produces non-empty string so fallback never triggers, and missing err.data?.code renders 'undefined: ...'; t(err.message) called on non-translation-key messages
findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 produces unhandled Prisma 500 error for orphan bookings instead of a graceful NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST TRPC error
No capacity check for seat-limited event types: handler blindly createMany's attendees beyond seatsPerTimeSlot limit and skips seat-attendee bookkeeping, potentially corrupting seat accounting
Any attendee (including unverified bookers) can add arbitrary guests to a booking, enabling an email/invite spam vector with no guest-count limit or rate limiting
BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive: incoming guest emails are not lowercased before comparison, allowing trivial blacklist bypass
Attendee dedup check (guest === attendee.email) is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee records for emails differing only in case
Team-admin authorization uses && instead of ||, requiring BOTH admin AND owner roles, so legitimate team admins are incorrectly denied access
Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, causing potential state divergence or wrong-account operations on the organizer's event
Booking ID enumeration possible via differential error responses (NOT_FOUND for nonexistent IDs vs FORBIDDEN for inaccessible IDs)
No check on booking.status allows guests to be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, sending misleading CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST emails for events that no longer exist
Duplicate guests within a single request create duplicate attendee rows because server-side schema does not enforce uniqueness (only client-side zod schema does)
Unhandled crash (500 error) when booking has null userId: findFirstOrThrow queries id: 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma error instead of a clean TRPC error
Unbounded `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts has no `.max()` cap, enabling authenticated resource-exhaustion via a single mutation with thousands of emails

Quadratic email fan-out in sendAddGuestsEmails: O(attendees) emails each embedding O(attendees) data, executed synchronously blocking the tRPC mutation; should cap guests and/or move email dispatch to a background job
Unused heavy `include` on booking query loads all credential rows (including secrets/tokens) for the booking owner even though credentials are never used in the handler
Blanket router invalidation `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` refetches all cached booking list queries instead of only the affected booking

Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, making isTeamAdminOrOwner always false since a role is never both ADMIN and OWNER, silently excluding team admins/owners from adding guests
renderEmail template registry not updated for new AttendeeAddGuestsEmail and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail classes, which would cause runtime rendering failures for every guest-add email
Server input schema lacks uniqueness validation on guests array that the client schema enforces, allowing non-UI callers to insert duplicate attendee rows via createMany
guests array has no max() bound on the new authenticated mutation, allowing email-bombing and long-running handlers via thousands of emails in one request
Guest email comparison is case-sensitive against attendees and blacklist, so Blacklisted@x.com bypasses the blacklist and A@x.com vs a@x.com produces duplicate attendees
Mutation returns hardcoded English string 'Guests added' instead of a translation key, breaking the convention where clients resolve messages via t()
findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws a raw Prisma P2025 error surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a typed NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST for orphaned bookings
Email send failures are silently swallowed by catch with console.log, returning success to the UI even when zero emails or ICS updates were delivered
add_members action is appended unconditionally to booking actions, appearing for cancelled/pending/rejected bookings and sending CONFIRMED ICS requests for events that aren't happening

Calendar update failure after DB write creates partial-failure state with non-idempotent retry: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called with no try/catch, so a calendar provider error throws after attendees are persisted; retry then fails with misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' since guests are already in booking.attendees

Email send failures silently swallowed: the catch block discards the error object, uses console.log instead of the structured logger, and returns success to the caller, so email delivery failures are unloggable, unalertable, and unretryable
Authorization logic bug: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only team owners pass the check and team admins are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN

Emails sent synchronously inline in the request handler via Promise.all with no timeout or queueing, so slow email providers stall the HTTP request until platform timeout while the DB write has already committed

Case-sensitive email deduplication and blacklist matching: guests are not normalized to lowercase, so adding User@Example.com when user@example.com exists creates duplicate attendee rows and differently-cased blacklisted addresses bypass the blacklist

No booking-status guard: guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, persisting them, updating the calendar, and sending emails with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST that re-confirm cancelled events in attendees' calendars

EventManager built from the requesting user's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar updates by attendees will fail or no-op against the organizer's calendar event

Unbounded guest list: guests array has no max() cap and no rate limiting or per-booking guest cap, allowing any permitted user (including attendees) to submit thousands of emails in one call as an email-amplification vector
Stale validation error state: isInvalidEmail is only reset by the cancel button, not on success, so the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is displayed the next time the dialog opens

Dead toast fallback and raw error codes surfaced to users: the template literal message is always truthy so the unable_to_add_guests fallback never executes, and t(err.message) is applied to non-translation keys missing from common.json, showing raw i18n keys and codes like 'FORBIDDEN:'
Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner check, denying team admins who should be able to manage bookings
Both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks run even when teamId is null, wasting DB calls
Blacklist comparison is not case-normalized on the guest side, allowing Guest@blocked.com to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing user@x.com to be re-added as User@x.com producing duplicate attendees
Client re-implements the server's Zod schema instead of importing it from the trpc router package
Server schema lacks the uniqueness constraint the client has, allowing duplicate attendee rows via non-UI callers
ZAddGuestsInputSchema is declared inside the component body and reconstructed on every render
Email-send failure is swallowed with a message-only console.log, discarding the error object with no observability
No validation of booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/pending bookings and sending misleading CONFIRMED emails
Hardcoded English string 'Remove email' in shared MultiEmail UI component instead of using useLocale()
MultiEmail imports from the @calcom/ui barrel that exports itself, creating fragile circular import coupling
Stale validation error persists across dialog reopens because isInvalidEmail is only reset by the Cancel button
readOnly prop of MultiEmail is dead code with no consumers, representing speculative generality
Authorization logic inverted: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner should be ||, so team admins are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN

Partial failure: DB write (attendees persisted) succeeds but calendar update can throw outside try/catch with no rollback, and retry is blocked by dedup filter returning misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'
Calendar update runs with the requester's credentials instead of the booking owner's, failing or targeting the wrong calendar when an attendee invokes the mutation
Server-side duplicate-email check is case-sensitive and doesn't dedupe within the input array, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails
Blacklist bypass via case mismatch: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is not, so 'Foo@blacklisted.com' bypasses the check
No check on booking status or time: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings, re-confirming cancelled events via ICS with status CONFIRMED
Silent email failure: errors swallowed with bare console.log, mutation returns success while guests may never receive invitations
Abuse vector: any attendee can add an unbounded number of guest emails with no verification, rate limit, or per-booking cap, enabling email-bombing
Seated bookings bypassed: raw attendees.createMany ignores seatsPerTimeSlot capacity and BookingSeat bookkeeping
Unhandled organizer lookup: findFirstOrThrow with id: 0 when booking.userId is null throws a raw Prisma error (500) instead of a meaningful TRPC error
Race condition on concurrent addGuests calls: non-transactional read-filter-createMany allows duplicate attendee inserts
Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is never cleared when user edits emails or reopens the dialog, so the warning banner persists

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial-failure dead end: DB write commits before calendar update; if updateCalendarAttendees throws, retry is impossible because dedupe filter strips already-persisted guests and throws misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error; no transaction or compensation path

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. There is no transaction/rollback around these steps. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will fail after the DB write has already committed, leaving the booking with the added guests but without the external calendar update/emails. On a subsequent retry with the same input, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees` (fetched at the start of the handler), so after the first partial success it will become empty and the handler will throw `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading and blocks a straightforward retry path. This failure mode is directly implied by the ordering and the `uniqueGuests.length === 0` error handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings: neither handler nor UI checks booking.status, sending CONFIRMED calendar invites for dead events and 'Guests Added' emails to organizer

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new `addGuestsHandler` loads the booking by `id` only and performs no check on `booking.status` (e.g., cancelled/rejected). It then updates attendees and unconditionally constructs a `CalendarEvent` without any status field and triggers `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates explicitly generate ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) and send “Guests Added” notifications regardless of booking state. The UI action to open `AddGuestsDialog` is also added without any status gating. Therefore, guests can be added and CONFIRMED invites/emails sent for non-active bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so attendees adding guests fail or silently no-op against the organizer's calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller) and `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The handler explicitly allows non-organizers (e.g., `isAttendee`) to add guests, but it never loads/uses the booking owner's (`booking.user`) credentials for `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Therefore, when an attendee invokes this mutation, the code attempts to update the organizer’s calendar event using the attendee’s credentials, which is likely to fail or no-op for the organizer’s connected calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||, collapsing to owner-only access and blocking team admins who are not owners
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner incorrectly requires both to be true, effectively excluding admins who aren’t owners; it should be || to allow either role.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive duplicate and blacklist checks: raw email comparison allows blacklist bypass via case variation and duplicate attendee records via case-differing emails; same flaw exists client-side in AddGuestsDialog
Server schema doesn't enforce email uniqueness within the guests array, so direct API callers can create duplicate attendee rows; uniqueness invariant only exists in client-side schema
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: the server-side logic/schema does not enforce or perform deduplication of repeated emails within the submitted guests list, so createMany (or equivalent) can insert duplicate attendee rows if a client submits duplicates. The candidate frames it as missing server-side uniqueness vs. client-side only, which matches the golden concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failures are swallowed: caught error is never logged with context, no error reporting fires, and handler returns success message regardless of email failure

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is ignored (no context/stack), and the handler continues to return `{ message: "Guests added" }` even if `sendAddGuestsEmails` fails, meaning email-send failures are effectively swallowed and not surfaced to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail flag is never reset on input change, success, or cancel, so the invalid-email error banner persists across fixes and dialog reopens

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is not reset when the user edits the emails via `MultiEmail` (`setMultiEmailValue` is called without touching `isInvalidEmail`). It is only reset on the explicit Cancel button. Also, `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`, and closing the dialog via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking outside/ESC) also won’t reset it. Since the dialog component remains mounted in `BookingListItem`, the error banner can persist after fixes and across dialog reopenings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error toast fallback is dead code: template literal always produces non-empty string so fallback never triggers, and missing err.data?.code renders 'undefined: ...'; t(err.message) called on non-translation-key messages

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds `message` as a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always returns a string (e.g., when `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes `'undefined: ...'`), so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` will never hit the fallback. This is a verifiable defect in the diff and can lead to user-facing toasts like `undefined: <something>` instead of the intended generic error. The part about `t(err.message)` possibly receiving non-translation-key strings is plausible but not strictly provable from the diff alone; however the dead-fallback/`undefined:` issue is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 produces unhandled Prisma 500 error for orphan bookings instead of a graceful NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined (the `|| 0` fallback explicitly anticipates a falsy value), this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "record not found" exception. The handler does not catch/translate that exception into a TRPCError (unlike the earlier explicit `NOT_FOUND` for the booking), so it would surface as an unhandled 500/internal error rather than a controlled NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No capacity check for seat-limited event types: handler blindly createMany's attendees beyond seatsPerTimeSlot limit and skips seat-attendee bookkeeping, potentially corrupting seat accounting

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler unconditionally appends new attendee rows via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` after filtering duplicates/blacklist, but it never checks `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or current attendee count) to ensure the booking still has available seats. The diff even propagates `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) but does not use them to enforce capacity before adding guests. For seat-limited event types, this allows adding attendees beyond the configured seat limit, which is a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any attendee (including unverified bookers) can add arbitrary guests to a booking, enabling an email/invite spam vector with no guest-count limit or rate limiting

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation is an `authedProcedure` and in `addGuestsHandler` it explicitly authorizes the caller if they are an attendee (`isAttendee` checks booking.attendees contains `user.email`). That means any authenticated attendee can submit an arbitrary `guests: string[]` (only validated as emails by `ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) and the handler will (1) write them to the booking via `createMany`, (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and (3) send emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no server-side cap on number of guests, no throttling/rate limiting logic, and no additional permission check restricting guest additions to organizer/admin-only. This creates a clear invite/email spam vector. The "unverified" part isn’t directly verifiable from this diff, but the core issue (attendees can add arbitrary guests with no limit) is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive: incoming guest emails are not lowercased before comparison, allowing trivial blacklist bypass
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue describe the same flaw: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but incoming guest emails are not, making the comparison effectively case-sensitive and allowing bypass via uppercase characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee dedup check (guest === attendee.email) is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee records for emails differing only in case

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the deduplication/filtering for new guests is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This is a strict, case-sensitive string comparison. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., lowercased) before comparison, adding `John@Example.com` when `john@example.com` already exists will pass the check and be treated as a new guest, potentially creating duplicate attendee records that differ only by email casing. The blacklist handling lowercases only the blacklist entries, but does not lowercase `guest`, further showing normalization is not consistently applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team-admin authorization uses && instead of ||, requiring BOTH admin AND owner roles, so legitimate team admins are incorrectly denied access

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check. Given the variable name and typical RBAC expectations (admin OR owner should be sufficient), this will incorrectly deny access to users who are admins but not owners (or owners but not admins), unless they also qualify as organizer/attendee. This is a concrete logic issue introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, causing potential state divergence or wrong-account operations on the organizer's event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via an `EventManager` instantiated with the *caller* (`...user`) and credentials fetched from the caller (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`). This happens even though the booking’s organizer is separately loaded (`organizer`) and the booking includes `user.credentials`. Since `addGuests` allows non-organizers (team admin/owner or an attendee) to call it, the mutation can update the booking’s calendar attendees using the wrong account’s credentials, which can fail or update the wrong calendar/integration state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking ID enumeration possible via differential error responses (NOT_FOUND for nonexistent IDs vs FORBIDDEN for inaccessible IDs)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the code first fetches the booking by `id` and immediately throws `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` if it doesn't exist. Only after that does it evaluate access control and throw `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN" })` when the booking exists but the caller is neither team admin/owner, organizer, nor attendee. Because the endpoint is an `authedProcedure` and accepts an arbitrary numeric `bookingId`, an authenticated caller can distinguish valid booking IDs from invalid ones by observing `NOT_FOUND` vs `FORBIDDEN`, enabling booking ID enumeration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking.status allows guests to be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, sending misleading CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST emails for events that no longer exist

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking and unconditionally allows updating `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(...)` with no check of any booking state/status (e.g., cancelled/rejected). Separately, the new email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` every time, regardless of the booking’s actual status. Therefore, if this mutation is invoked for a cancelled/rejected booking, it can add guests and send “CONFIRMED” update emails for an event that is no longer active, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate guests within a single request create duplicate attendee rows because server-side schema does not enforce uniqueness (only client-side zod schema does)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. On the server, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the `guests` array itself (e.g., `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` will pass the filter if not already an attendee). Those duplicates are then inserted via `attendees.createMany` with `data: guestsFullDetails`, which would create duplicate attendee rows unless the DB enforces a unique constraint (not shown in the diff). Client-side `AddGuestsDialog` does have a uniqueness refine, but that can be bypassed by calling the endpoint directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled crash (500 error) when booking has null userId: findFirstOrThrow queries id: 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma error instead of a clean TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined (the code explicitly anticipates this by `|| 0`), the query becomes `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (P2025/not found). That exception is not caught and is not converted to a `TRPCError`, so it will surface as an internal error rather than a clean, intentional TRPC response. This matches the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts has no `.max()` cap, enabling authenticated resource-exhaustion via a single mutation with thousands of emails

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and no `.max()`/size limit. The new `addGuests` mutation is `authedProcedure` and the handler uses the array to (a) build `guestsFullDetails`, (b) `createMany` attendees in the DB, (c) rebuild attendee translation payloads, (d) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and (e) send emails to all attendees (`sendAddGuestsEmails`) — all proportional to the size of `guests` / resulting attendees. Since any organizer/attendee can invoke it and the UI (`MultiEmail`) allows adding arbitrary numbers, a single authenticated request with thousands of emails can trigger large DB writes and outbound email/update work, i.e., a verifiable resource-exhaustion vector stemming from the lack of an input cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Quadratic email fan-out in sendAddGuestsEmails: O(attendees) emails each embedding O(attendees) data, executed synchronously blocking the tRPC mutation; should cap guests and/or move email dispatch to a background job
Unused heavy `include` on booking query loads all credential rows (including secrets/tokens) for the booking owner even though credentials are never used in the handler

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, but the handler never references `booking.user.credentials`. Instead it fetches credentials separately via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and passes those into `new EventManager(...)`. So the `credentials: true` include is redundant in this diff and will cause extra rows/fields to be loaded from the DB unnecessarily.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blanket router invalidation `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` refetches all cached booking list queries instead of only the affected booking

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the mutation `onSuccess` calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();`. In tRPC React Query utils, calling `invalidate()` at the router level (`viewer.bookings`) invalidates *all* cached queries under that router (e.g., booking lists, booking details, etc.), not just the specific booking that was updated (`bookingId`). This matches the finding: it will trigger broader refetching than necessary and could be replaced with a more targeted invalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, making isTeamAdminOrOwner always false since a role is never both ADMIN and OWNER, silently excluding team admins/owners from adding guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to satisfy both checks. Given the variable name and its use in the permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`), this is very likely intended to allow either team admins or team owners. As written, a user who is an admin but not an owner would be denied from adding guests (overly restrictive authorization). Whether it is *always* false depends on how those helpers treat owners, but the core issue (AND vs OR changes authorization semantics) is real and present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: renderEmail template registry not updated for new AttendeeAddGuestsEmail and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail classes, which would cause runtime rendering failures for every guest-add email

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* update the React email template export registry: `packages/emails/src/templates/index.ts` now exports both `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. The NodeMailer classes (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`) call `renderEmail("OrganizerAddGuestsEmail"|"AttendeeAddGuestsEmail", ...)`, and those names are now present in the templates index. So the claim that the template registry was not updated (and would cause runtime rendering failures) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server input schema lacks uniqueness validation on guests array that the client schema enforces, allowing non-UI callers to insert duplicate attendee rows via createMany

adjudication.rationale: The client dialog validates uniqueness via a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema using `.refine()` on the emails array, but the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in `addGuests.schema.ts` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the `guests` input array. As a result, a non-UI caller can send duplicate emails, `uniqueGuests` will still contain duplicates, and `createMany` will attempt to insert duplicate attendee rows for the same booking (or trigger a DB error if a unique constraint exists, which is not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: guests array has no max() bound on the new authenticated mutation, allowing email-bombing and long-running handlers via thousands of emails in one request

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the new authenticated mutation input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`/length limit. In `addGuestsHandler`, those emails are used to `createMany` attendees and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` sends emails per attendee (`calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`), which can scale to thousands if a client submits a huge `guests` array. This enables an authorized caller (organizer/attendee/team admin) to trigger large DB writes and mass outbound email sending in a single request (email-bombing/DoS risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest email comparison is case-sensitive against attendees and blacklist, so Blacklisted@x.com bypasses the blacklist and A@x.com vs a@x.com produces duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased (`map(...toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This allows bypass via different casing (e.g., `Blacklisted@x.com`). Similarly, duplicate prevention compares `guest === attendee.email` and the client-side uniqueness check uses `new Set(emails)`, both case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` and `a@x.com` can be treated as distinct and added as duplicate attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutation returns hardcoded English string 'Guests added' instead of a translation key, breaking the convention where clients resolve messages via t()

adjudication.rationale: The handler `addGuestsHandler` does return `{ message: "Guests added" }` (hardcoded English) in the diff. However, in the newly added client code (`AddGuestsDialog`) the success UX does not use this return value; it always shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` and invalidates the cache. Nothing in the diff demonstrates that the returned `message` is consumed by clients via `t()`, so claiming it "breaks the convention where clients resolve messages via t()" is not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff (it’s at most an optional consistency/i18n nit if someone later displays that message).

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws a raw Prisma P2025 error surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a typed NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST for orphaned bookings

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` with no error handling. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined (or points to a deleted user), `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (commonly Prisma P2025), which will bubble up as an untyped error (TRPC INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) rather than the handler’s explicit `TRPCError` NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST patterns. This is a concrete failure path introduced/visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are silently swallowed by catch with console.log, returning success to the UI even when zero emails or ICS updates were delivered

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not rethrow or return an error. The handler then proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" }`, so the UI will see success even if email sending fails. (The calendar update `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` is not in that `try/catch`, so that part would still fail loudly, but email delivery failures are definitely swallowed.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members action is appended unconditionally to booking actions, appearing for cancelled/pending/rejected bookings and sending CONFIRMED ICS requests for events that aren't happening

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an "add_members" action to the `actions` array in `BookingListItem` with no gating on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected/pending). Separately, the new `addGuests` mutation/handler does not check any booking status before updating attendees and sending emails. The new email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` unconditionally. Therefore, it is verifiable from the diff that the UI action can appear for non-active bookings and the backend can send CONFIRMED calendar invites even if the booking is cancelled or otherwise not happening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update failure after DB write creates partial-failure state with non-idempotent retry: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called with no try/catch, so a calendar provider error throws after attendees are persisted; retry then fails with misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' since guests are already in booking.attendees

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuestsHandler` the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch/transaction/rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (calendar provider/API failure), the mutation will error after the DB write, leaving a partial-success state (attendees stored but calendar not updated and `sendAddGuestsEmails` not reached). On a client retry, the handler refetches the booking and computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out any emails already in `booking.attendees`; that can yield `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and it then throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading because the emails were already added by the prior partial attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures silently swallowed: the catch block discards the error object, uses console.log instead of the structured logger, and returns success to the caller, so email delivery failures are unloggable, unalertable, and unretryable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. The caught `err` is ignored (not logged/recorded), `console.log` is used instead of any structured logging, and the caller cannot detect failure, making delivery failures effectively silent and not retryable from the API perspective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic bug: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only team owners pass the check and team admins are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to pass. The variable name and subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`) indicate the intent is to allow either admins or owners; with `&&`, a team admin who is not also an owner will be incorrectly denied unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Emails sent synchronously inline in the request handler via Promise.all with no timeout or queueing, so slow email providers stall the HTTP request until platform timeout while the DB write has already committed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after the booking attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update(...)`, the handler does `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (inside a try/catch). `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts` builds an array of email send promises and then `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. This means the TRPC/HTTP request will not resolve until all email sends complete; there is no queueing/background job and no timeout/circuit breaker shown in the diff. If the email provider is slow/hangs, the request can stall or time out even though the DB update has already committed, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email deduplication and blacklist matching: guests are not normalized to lowercase, so adding User@Example.com when user@example.com exists creates duplicate attendee rows and differently-cased blacklisted addresses bypass the blacklist

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, both the existing-attendee check and blacklist check are case-sensitive: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase while `guest` is not, so a differently-cased blacklisted email (e.g. `User@Example.com`) will bypass the blacklist. Likewise, if an attendee already exists as `user@example.com`, adding `User@Example.com` will not be detected as a duplicate and will be inserted via `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows differing only by case (unless prevented elsewhere by a DB constraint not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status guard: guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, persisting them, updating the calendar, and sending emails with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST that re-confirm cancelled events in attendees' calendars

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates `booking.attendees` and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` for any booking found by id, but it never checks the booking's status (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED). The newly added email templates generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (both in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so invoking this on a cancelled/rejected booking would still persist new attendees, push calendar updates, and send (re-)confirmation-like invites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager built from the requesting user's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar updates by attendees will fail or no-op against the organizer's calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation permits non-organizers to add guests (it allows if isAttendee is true). However the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` where `user`/`ctx.user` is the requesting user, not the booking organizer (`booking.userId`). The handler even loads `booking.user` with `credentials` but never uses them. If an attendee triggers this mutation, the EventManager will be configured with the attendee’s credentials, so it cannot reliably update the organizer’s destination calendar event referenced by the booking, leading to a likely no-op/failure of the intended calendar attendee update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guest list: guests array has no max() cap and no rate limiting or per-booking guest cap, allowing any permitted user (including attendees) to submit thousands of emails in one call as an email-amplification vector

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` and the handler performs `createMany` for all `uniqueGuests` and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends an email per attendee (plus organizer/team emails). Authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call this endpoint. Nothing in the diff enforces a per-booking/per-call guest cap or otherwise bounds the size of `guests`, so a permitted user can submit a very large array and trigger mass DB writes + outbound email sends in one request (amplification risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale validation error state: isInvalidEmail is only reset by the cancel button, not on success, so the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is displayed the next time the dialog opens

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when schema validation fails in `handleAdd()`, and it is only reset in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). In the mutation `onSuccess`, the dialog is closed and `multiEmailValue` is reset, but `isInvalidEmail` is not reset. Therefore, if a user previously triggered the invalid state and later successfully adds guests (or simply closes/reopens without hitting Cancel), reopening the dialog will still render the error block (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`), showing a stale validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead toast fallback and raw error codes surfaced to users: the template literal message is always truthy so the unable_to_add_guests fallback never executes, and t(err.message) is applied to non-translation keys missing from common.json, showing raw i18n keys and codes like 'FORBIDDEN:'

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`’s `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (e.g. `"undefined: ..."`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback. Also, the toast explicitly prefixes `err.data?.code` (e.g. `FORBIDDEN`, `BAD_REQUEST`), so raw TRPC error codes will be shown to end users. The claim about missing translation keys is not fully provable from the diff alone, but the dead fallback and surfacing raw codes are directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner check, denying team admins who should be able to manage bookings

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass, which contradicts the variable name and typical authorization intent (admin OR owner). As a result, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail the later permission check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`) and be incorrectly denied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks run even when teamId is null, wasting DB calls

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. When `booking.eventType?.teamId` is `null`/`undefined` (e.g., non-team/personal bookings), both functions are still awaited with `0`, which will trigger whatever DB/query work those helpers do despite there being no real team to check. This matches the finding of wasted calls when `teamId` is null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is not case-normalized on the guest side, allowing Guest@blocked.com to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` strings are compared as-is: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (and Zod `email()` does not force lowercase), an input like `Guest@blocked.com` would not match `guest@blocked.com` in the blacklist and could bypass the block. The same non-normalized comparison is also used against existing attendee emails (`guest === attendee.email`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing user@x.com to be re-added as User@x.com producing duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, duplicates are filtered with a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` are normalized (e.g., lowercased), `user@x.com` and `User@x.com` will not match and can both be added. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` also uses `new Set(emails)` which is likewise case-sensitive, so it won’t prevent this either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client re-implements the server's Zod schema instead of importing it from the trpc router package

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the client defines a Zod schema only to validate the local `multiEmailValue` (a `string[]`) and additionally enforces uniqueness via `.refine()`. The server TRPC input schema added in `addGuests.schema.ts` is a different shape (`{ bookingId: number; guests: string[] }`) and does not include the uniqueness refinement. So the client is not “re-implementing the server’s Zod schema”; it’s doing separate UI-side validation for a different value shape. This is not a clear defect introduced by the diff (the server still validates emails and enforces meaningful constraints in the handler).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema lacks the uniqueness constraint the client has, allowing duplicate attendee rows via non-UI callers

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The client-side dialog validates uniqueness via `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`, but the server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness check. In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the `guests` input itself, so `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` will remain duplicated and be passed to `attendees.createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows (depending on DB constraints). This makes duplicates possible via non-UI callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is declared inside the component body and reconstructed on every render

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` is indeed declared inside the `AddGuestsDialog` component, so it will be recreated on every render. However, in this diff it’s only used imperatively in `handleAdd()` via `safeParse`, and nothing depends on its identity (no hook deps, memoization, etc.). This is at most a minor performance/style nit, not a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failure is swallowed with a message-only console.log, discarding the error object with no observability

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is ignored (not logged, rethrown, or reported), and the handler still returns success, so any email-send failure is effectively swallowed with only a generic console message and no error details/observability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/pending bookings and sending misleading CONFIRMED emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` (new file), the booking is fetched and updated without any check of `booking.status` (or equivalent cancelled/pending flags). The handler will always proceed to `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, and the email templates hardcode ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` (see `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). This means authorized users can add guests to cancelled/pending bookings and recipients may receive misleading "CONFIRMED" calendar updates/emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded English string 'Remove email' in shared MultiEmail UI component instead of using useLocale()

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added shared UI component `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the Tooltip uses a hardcoded English string: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`. The component already imports and uses `useLocale()` for other labels (e.g., `t("add_another")`), so this is a verifiable i18n/localization defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail imports from the @calcom/ui barrel that exports itself, creating fragile circular import coupling
Stale validation error persists across dialog reopens because isInvalidEmail is only reset by the Cancel button

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in `AddGuestsDialog`: `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd()`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. The dialog can be closed via `Dialog`’s `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` (e.g., clicking outside/ESC), which does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Since the component remains mounted in `BookingListItem`, reopening the dialog will preserve `isInvalidEmail === true`, causing the validation error UI to appear immediately (stale error).

adjudication_records.issue_text: readOnly prop of MultiEmail is dead code with no consumers, representing speculative generality

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `MultiEmail` with a `readOnly` prop and it is immediately consumed by `AddGuestsDialog` as `readOnly={false}`, so the prop is not “dead code with no consumers.” While the `readOnly=true` branch currently has no usage shown in this diff, that is not a verifiable defect (it’s an API/design choice, not a correctness/security bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic inverted: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner should be ||, so team admins are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to pass the permission check. Given the variable name and typical role semantics (admin OR owner should be sufficient), a user who is only an admin (not owner) will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and, if not also the booking organizer or an attendee, will hit the `FORBIDDEN` branch. This is a concrete, verifiable logic error introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial failure: DB write (attendees persisted) succeeds but calendar update can throw outside try/catch with no rollback, and retry is blocked by dedup filter returning misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. That calendar update is *outside* the `try/catch` (only `sendAddGuestsEmails` is guarded), so if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails after the DB write, leaving the DB changed without any rollback/transaction. On a retry with the same guest emails, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, resulting in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and a `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading in this scenario and effectively blocks a straightforward retry for calendar sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs with the requester's credentials instead of the booking owner's, failing or targeting the wrong calendar when an attendee invokes the mutation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar sync is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` where `eventManager` is constructed from `ctx.user` (the caller) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The handler allows non-organizer attendees to call the mutation (`isAttendee` grants access). When an attendee invokes it, the calendar update will use the attendee’s connected calendar credentials rather than the booking owner/organizer’s credentials (even though the booking query includes `booking.user.credentials`, they are not used). This can fail (attendee has no integration/permissions) or update the wrong account’s calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side duplicate-email check is case-sensitive and doesn't dedupe within the input array, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guests.filter(...)` only against existing `booking.attendees` and a blacklist. It does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself, so an input like `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` will keep both entries and pass `uniqueGuests.length > 0`, then `createMany` will attempt to create duplicate attendee records. Additionally, comparisons are case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`) and the blacklist is lowercased while `guest` is not, so emails differing only by case can bypass both checks and be treated as distinct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case mismatch: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is not, so 'Foo@blacklisted.com' bypasses the check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` values from `input.guests` are used as-is in the check: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (nor otherwise normalized), a blacklisted address can bypass the filter by changing case (e.g., `Foo@blacklisted.com` vs `foo@blacklisted.com`). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking status or time: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings, re-confirming cancelled events via ICS with status CONFIRMED

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates attendees and sends calendar emails without any guard on booking lifecycle. It fetches the booking and checks only permissions, then always updates attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)`), calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends emails. There is no check for booking being cancelled/rejected/expired or for `booking.startTime/endTime` being in the past. Additionally, the new ICS payloads in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts` hardcode `status: "CONFIRMED"`, so invoking this on a cancelled booking could send a CONFIRMED invite/update, effectively re-confirming in recipients' calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent email failure: errors swallowed with bare console.log, mutation returns success while guests may never receive invitations

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, sending the notification emails is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues. The handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless of whether `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` succeeded. This makes email delivery failures non-fatal and effectively hidden from the caller/UI, so guests (and organizers) may not receive the intended email notifications even though the mutation reports success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Abuse vector: any attendee can add an unbounded number of guest emails with no verification, rate limit, or per-booking cap, enabling email-bombing

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation allows any booking attendee to add arbitrary guest email addresses: `isAttendee` is treated as authorized (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ... FORBIDDEN`). The input schema only validates `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max length or per-booking cap, and the handler does `createMany` with whatever number of emails are provided. It then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which sends emails to organizer/team members and all attendees, creating an obvious abuse path for sending a large volume of emails to arbitrary recipients, with no verification, rate limiting, or bounding shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seated bookings bypassed: raw attendees.createMany ignores seatsPerTimeSlot capacity and BookingSeat bookkeeping

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` after filtering duplicates/blacklist, but it never checks `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or current attendee count) before adding. Since the handler itself reads `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the CalendarEvent, it’s aware of “seated” semantics but does no capacity enforcement, meaning seated/capacity-limited bookings can be exceeded by adding guests. The claim about specific “BookingSeat bookkeeping” isn’t shown in the diff, but the core issue (no seat/capacity enforcement when adding attendees) is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled organizer lookup: findFirstOrThrow with id: 0 when booking.userId is null throws a raw Prisma error (500) instead of a meaningful TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. The use of `booking.userId || 0` indicates `booking.userId` may be `null/undefined` in some cases; when that happens, the query becomes `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "not found" error. Unlike the earlier explicit `if (!booking) throw new TRPCError(...)`, this thrown Prisma error is not converted to a `TRPCError`, so it will surface as an unhandled/internal server error (500) rather than a meaningful TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition on concurrent addGuests calls: non-transactional read-filter-createMany allows duplicate attendee inserts

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first reads the booking (including current attendees), computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against `booking.attendees`, and then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})`. Because the “check” (filter) and the “insert” are not done atomically (no transaction/locking and no `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })`), two concurrent addGuests calls can both decide the same email is not yet an attendee and both attempt to insert it. Depending on DB constraints (not shown here), this can either create duplicate attendee rows or cause one request to fail with a uniqueness violation. Either way, the diff introduces a real check-then-insert race window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is never cleared when user edits emails or reopens the dialog, so the warning banner persists

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared when the user edits emails via `MultiEmail` (`setMultiEmailValue` only) nor when the dialog is reopened (the component stays mounted under `BookingListItem`, and `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` does not reset `isInvalidEmail`). Additionally, `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`, so the warning can persist across reopenings.
